Chaos the Cancer Lion

By: Sasha OLD | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A lion undergoes radiation treatment for cancer at Meulmed hospital to save his life.

Unique Selling Point:
We will have this story exclusively. They are sick of the other media - they all just pitched up at the hospital and forced their way into theatre. It was very chaotic, but they are willing to let us tell the entire story from A TO Z. In a South Africa first, possibly a world first, an adult lion is being treated at a hospital for cancer. Chaos was quite a ladies man, until he met Tequila, who is almost 2 years older than him – the only female he has ever mated with and they have been inseparable since introduced. He is very protective of her, and when she does come into heat he will not let anyone near their housing. They did have three littres, Amber - the one female is still at the zoo, and the other cubs went to the Sao Paulo zoo in Brazil, after that there have been no other littre’s. They want to keep his sperm on file so that there is a mixture of different lion sperm available, although Matty says there is no lion breeding program in South Africa like there is with Cheetah’s and Leopards. (From Kara: "Its not that there isn’t a breeding programme, the problem is that even if DNA is banked at bio labs, there is still no proof needed to export cats such as with Cheetahs. There is not enough effort being put into the conservation of these majestic cats. We have not bio banked any of Chaos’ sperm yet.") Chaos and Teuqila are currently retired animals – who live in a lovely large cage at the back of the zoo where the public are not allowed. When animals become older and no longer enjoy the public – this is where they are brought to. Wild male lions usually only live to 10-12 years, while in captivity they can live from 20-24 years old.

Summary:
Chaos is a 16 year old male tawny lion who has grown up in Midrand’s Lory Park Zoo. Weighing in at close to 300kg, this massive specimen came to the zoo in 2002 when he was a few weeks old. Back then there was no lion bone trade or lion pet industry – or the problems we currently have of a massive lion population in captivity in South Africa – which results in many going into the canned hunting industry. Lory park is a private zoo, that began when it’s owners Matty and Eddy van Eck wanted to share his private collection of animals - mostly birds with the public for educational purposes. They are a facility that brings in veterinary training students from overseas, and school students wanting to learn about animals up close and personal. They do not breed their animals now, but keep the females on contraception and the males are given vasectomy’s because this is better for the animal rather than outright neutering. This keeps the animals healthier – so they don’t gain excessive weight, and allows them to keep their natural tendency’s rather than just neutering them because it makes it easier for them to be handled. (Kara: "The reason that we use vasectomy is it is much less invasive and unfortunately the contraceptive implant has many negative affects on female cats. It also ensures that hormone levels aren’t affected.") Lory park was originally a bird park, based on the Lorikeet parrot – but it has grown to incorporate many other animals ranging from big cats, apes, reptiles and birds. Matty doesn’t see the animals as pets but as ambassadors for their kind and naturally has a deep love and respect for them - they have many conservation projects and work with Onderstepoort.

Further information:
A few years ago one of their female tigers got cancer of her ovary’s and they tried all the veterinary options available, gave her life saving surgery, but in the end she didn’t survive (From Kara: unfortunately the cancer spread after a year and we made the very hard decision to let her go as her quality of life was being affected). When Chaos was diagnosed with skin cancer earlier this year, they were worried of losing him, most especially because of his bond with Tequila. He has skin cancer on his leg and nose, as lions love to lie in the sun. They were able to operate and remove much of the cancer in his leg because there’s lots of tissue, but his nose was a different matter. If they had left it, it would have eaten away his bones and face – causing him much suffering. Considering all the factors, what to do was a difficult decision, Matty and manager of the zoo Kara Heynis decided to try something different – radiation cancer treatment at a normal human hospital – rather than at a veterinary facility – mostly because Radiation on a male adult lion has never been tried before. (kara: "With regards to Chaos’ treatment we never decided to try something different. The veterinary team suggested that radiation would be the best way to treat his form of cancer and we proceeded with their recommendations after much consideration. This was a decision made by the parks management") This would be expensive, but as it’s a private facility they would get support from their private donors. Eddy had to make the decision with a lot of care, because once they did this for one animal, they would need to do it for every other, and they needed to make sure it wasn’t going to be too expensive that would result in the zoo closing its doors. They also wanted to give Chaos and Tequila time together, as they are inseparable, her wellbeing was also taken into consideration.
This is the first time in South Africa that a male lion is being treated in a human hospital with a human doctor, and his oncologist at Meulmed private clinic in Pretoria Dr Ingo De Mûelenaere said after his first two treatments, the patient is doing very well. Overseen by Onderstepoort teaching sciences head Veterinarian Dr. Katja Koeppel, Chaos’ treatment is potentially a world first (although no one really knows – but I can’t find any other lion on the internet). His cancer treatment has gone viral with his pictures showing up in Asia, Australia, America and Europe! Dr. Koeppal and her team ensure that they use a light sedative on Chaos, because of his age, and because anaesthesia is always a concern for any animal, and they assist in transferring him from his sick bay at Lory Park, to Meulmed in Pretoria. Meulmed have been very accommodating, in that they close down their oncology bay during his visits. He is quite the attraction when he arrives, as you need to somehow get the big boy all the way onto the table, sedate him long enough to administer the radiation and then get him back into his personalized carrier – all as quick as possible so as to keep his stress down. We will be with him on his 3rd visit, after that he only has one more. After every radiation treatment the patient has made a full recovery, and is eating very well. Lions in captivity mostly die because they have kidney failure, but besides the cancer, Chaos has some of the most healthy bloods, and has been constantly monitored. We would tell Chaos’ personal story and show how difficult it is to give a fully grown male lion the best care he deserves.




Extra Budget Items:
As there is a light sedative, if Chaos’ anxiety level increases the he won’t go under, so they’ve asked us not to be around him until after he’s out. Which is fine with us… we are welcome to film the entire process from start to finish, and I have secured Russell Bergh who is an animal specialist videographer who also used to be a Kruger ranger. They have also asked that we limit the number of people – I thought then potentially the best thing for us to do is to film half day from 3-7pm Wednesday next week (lions are better in the afternoon, by then Tequila won’t be on heat). They have housed Chaos is a special garden with lots of shade, lions love the sun, but because of his skin cancer and nose, they want him to be exposed to the sun as little as possible. We are welcome to go into his cage – heck no. and heck no is the presenter. Russell can do what he wants, but I choose life. I’m happy with just getting shots of him from a safe distance with a cage in-between lol. We can do Matty and Kara’s interviews by his cage, the vet’s interview on the day, and the oncologists interview on the day. There are only 4 interviews – which I think is fine for a 6 minute story. So it would be a day and a half shoot – if that’s fine? But I would ask that we only have the soundman on the half day at the facility, on the day of the actual moving etc it will just be me presenter and cameraman – so that there are fewer people. I will take full responsibility like I did in the pedigree dog story where we had no audio issues.

Press Release:


Chaos the Lion
His name is Chaos, a 16-year-old full-grown, hand-reared lion with skin cancer. Now, in a first for South Africa, he’s undergoing controversial lifesaving radiation treatment - at a private hospital for humans in Pretoria. Carte Blanche goes behind the scenes as the king of the jungle takes centre stage in the oncology unit.
Producer: Sasha Schwendenwein
Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


DEREK: THIS IS THE LORI PARK ZOO SITUATED BETWEEN JOBURG AND PRETORIA. ORIGINALLY A BIRD PARK NAMED AFTER THESE VERY ENTHUSIASTIC TWEETERS THE LORIKEETS. TWENTY YEARS LATER IT HAS A VARIETY OF REPTILES, APES AND BIG CATS ONE OF THEM VERY FAMOUS….
Upsound: “ROARRRR!”
Matty: “He's got a big personality, and the warmest eyes you've ever seen.”
It’s hard to believe Lori Park Zoo’s co-owner Matty van Eck is talking about a full grown tawny lion named Chaos.
Matty: “Chaos is our oldest lion. He's 16 years old now and he's just been such a great ambassador for the zoo.”
Chaos lives a quiet life in the retirement section of the zoo with Tequila, his soulmate of 15 years.
Matty: “Tequila is Chaos’ love of his life. When you look at them, the love that emanates from them it's beautiful.”
But then came the bad news for the loving couple.
Matty: “He started with the lesions in early April, and that came up with skin cancer which was caused by the sun.”
Kara: “We have two lesions on his nose and we had one lesion on his leg, that one has been removed surgically.”
Managing his recovery is Lory Park’s Zoologist Kara Heynis, who already has her hands full with these rescued flamingo’s.
Kara: “That will eventually attack the bone structure in the face which would eat away at the bone. So it would be incredibly painful.”
Therefore, Chaos’ only option was radiation at a hospital - a South African first.
Matty: “We’re treating him in a human hospital simply because there are no veterinary practices that have the proper equipment to treat him.”
Carte Blanche followed the third of four radiation treatments which altogether will cost R50,000. Dr Katja Koeppel, who teaches Veterinary Science at Onderstepoort, prepares the sedative in order to transport Chaos to the hospital.
DEREK: THIS IS THE VITAL PART OF THE OPERATION TO ACTUALLY GET TO DART CHAOS. AND WE SAW EARLIER HE'S NOT IN A VERY GOOD MOOD. I THINK HE KNOWS. TODAY'S A BIG DAY.
Upsound: “DART...Chaos roars…”
Katja: looks at angry lion… “That’s What he thinks of me!”
Derek: “Was it a good shot?”
Katja: “Sort of, it’s nice in his butt!”
Derek: “Matty, I see you’re quite emotional right now?”
Matty: “It's always just a huge big risk every time, I don't like doing this to him but it's tough love.”
DEREK: CHAOS IS OUT FOR THE COUNT,AND HOPEFULLY THE NEXT FEW HOURS.
Katja: “So it's quite time sensitive that we are fast because our anesthetic from darting to reversal was about two hours. We need to keep his airway open. We need to make sure his heart rate and his respiration are good.”
Derek: “And that he doesn't wake up in the middle of the hospital?”
Katja: “That would be one of the key points, not for me so much, but I think the hospital would appreciate it.”
DEREK: THIS MUST BE THE HEAVIEST PATIENT. THIS GURNEYS EVER CARRIED AROUND 260 KILOS. THAT'S ABOUT TWO AND A HALF WATTS.
Derek: “What have you done here?”
Katja: “Chaos this is also one of the tumors. This one we removed by surgery and he licked the stitches out.”
He’s carefully loaded into a crate, and one of the veterinary students will monitor him during the drive.
Vet student: “Well you need to monitor a heart rate pulse so the oxygenation of the blood and temperature.”
Derek: “And if he starts waking up?”
Vet student: “Then you have to give him top up drugs.”
40 minutes later Chaos is offloaded at the private cancer clinic in Pretoria where he’s met by his Oncologist Dr. Ingo de Meulenaere.
Ingo: “For these superficial lesions we use electrons to do the treatment with and that causes the reaction in the tissue that kills the cancerous cells.”
His head is secured so he can undergo 6 minutes of radiation on each of the two lesions on his nose...
Everyone must wait outside to avoid the radiation...
Derek: “Katja what’s the problem there?”
Katja: “I need him to be asleep for a little bit longer. We are now within our hour and 53 minutes.”
The pressure pushes the team to move quickly for his second application...
And once that’s done there’s the final rush to put him back in his crate so Dr. Koeppel can administer the antidote…
They’ve really pushed the 2 hour time limit…
A great sigh of relief from everyone involved as Chaos blinks...
Ingo: “He’s an absolutely wonderful response. The tumors have basically melted away and he's had very little side effects
Derek: “I'm sure you'll be growling in that moment. Shall we go have a look.”
They close the crate allowing him time to rest for the drive home…
MONTAGE…
An hour later his crate is opened...
DEREK: ANOTHER DAY IN THE LIFE OF CHAOS, AND IRONICALLY IT’S RUN QUITE SMOOTHLY THANKS TO SOME VERY DEDICATED PROFESSIONALS, AND I CAN TELL YOU THAT SOMEBODY IS VERY RELIEVED.
Matty: “It's always a relief when it's over and done with. So. Yeah one more lift and then we nearly done.”
DEREK: THERE'S BEEN A BACKLASH FROM SOME PEOPLE WHO SAY THERE'S NOT SUFFICIENT RADIATION TREATMENT FOR PEOPLE IN SOUTH AFRICA, WHY ARE THEY TREATING A LION? AND THEY MAY HAVE A POINT.
Matty: “Chaos is not by no means taking somebody’s place in a queue. We've made sure that we can provide for our animals if something like this should happen.”
All that’s left is for Chaos to go sleep off the anesthetics’ effects. 06:04

Upsound: “DART...Chaos roars…” Katja: looks at angry lion… “That’s What he thinks of me!” Derek: “Was it a good shot?” Katja: “Sort of, it’s nice in his butt!” Derek: “Matty, I see you’re quite emotional right now?” Matty: “It's always just a huge big risk every time, I don't like doing this to him but it's tough love.” DEREK: CHAOS IS OUT FOR THE COUNT,AND HOPEFULLY THE NEXT FEW HOURS. Katja: “So it's quite time sensitive that we are fast because our anesthetic from darting to reversal was about two hours. We need to keep his airway open. We need to make sure his heart rate and his respiration are good.” Derek: “And that he doesn't wake up in the middle of the hospital?” Katja: “That would be one of the key points, not for me so much, but I think the hospital would appreciate it.” DEREK: THIS MUST BE THE HEAVIEST PATIENT. THIS GURNEYS EVER CARRIED AROUND 260 KILOS. THAT'S ABOUT TWO AND A HALF WATTS. Derek: “What have you done here?” Katja: “Chaos this is also one of the tumors. This one we removed by surgery and he licked the stitches out.” He’s carefully loaded into a crate, and one of the veterinary students will monitor him during the drive. Vet student: “Well you need to monitor a heart rate pulse so the oxygenation of the blood and temperature.” Derek: “And if he starts waking up?” Vet student: “Then you have to give him top up drugs.” 40 minutes later Chaos is offloaded at the private cancer clinic in Pretoria where he’s met by his Oncologist Dr. Ingo de Meulenaere. Ingo: “For these superficial lesions we use electrons to do the treatment with and that causes the reaction in the tissue that kills the cancerous cells.” His head is secured so he can undergo 6 minutes of radiation on each of the two lesions on his nose... Everyone must wait outside to avoid the radiation... Derek: “Katja what’s the problem there?” Katja: “I need him to be asleep for a little bit longer. We are now within our hour and 53 minutes.” The pressure pushes the team to move quickly for his second application... And once that’s done there’s the final rush to put him back in his crate so Dr. Koeppel can administer the antidote… They’ve really pushed the 2 hour time limit… A great sigh of relief from everyone involved as Chaos blinks... Ingo: “He’s an absolutely wonderful response. The tumors have basically melted away and he's had very little side effects Derek: “I'm sure you'll be growling in that moment. Shall we go have a look.” They close the crate allowing him time to rest for the drive home… MONTAGE… An hour later his crate is opened... DEREK: ANOTHER DAY IN THE LIFE OF CHAOS, AND IRONICALLY IT’S RUN QUITE SMOOTHLY THANKS TO SOME VERY DEDICATED PROFESSIONALS, AND I CAN TELL YOU THAT SOMEBODY IS VERY RELIEVED. Matty: “It's always a relief when it's over and done with. So. Yeah one more lift and then we nearly done.” DEREK: THERE'S BEEN A BACKLASH FROM SOME PEOPLE WHO SAY THERE'S NOT SUFFICIENT RADIATION TREATMENT FOR PEOPLE IN SOUTH AFRICA, WHY ARE THEY TREATING A LION? AND THEY MAY HAVE A POINT. Matty: “Chaos is not by no means taking somebody’s place in a queue. We've made sure that we can provide for our animals if something like this should happen.” All that’s left is for Chaos to go sleep off the anesthetics’ effects. 06:04

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A lion undergoes radiation treatment for cancer at Meulmed hospital to save his life.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We will have this story exclusively. They are sick of the other media - they all just pitched up at the hospital and forced their way into theatre. It was very chaotic, but they are willing to let us tell the entire story from A TO Z. In a South Africa first, possibly a world first, an adult lion is being treated at a hospital for cancer. Chaos was quite a ladies man, until he met Tequila, who is almost 2 years older than him – the only female he has ever mated with and they have been inseparable since introduced. He is very protective of her, and when she does come into heat he will not let anyone near their housing. They did have three littres, Amber - the one female is still at the zoo, and the other cubs went to the Sao Paulo zoo in Brazil, after that there have been no other littre’s. They want to keep his sperm on file so that there is a mixture of different lion sperm available, although Matty says there is no lion breeding program in South Africa like there is with Cheetah’s and Leopards. (From Kara: "Its not that there isn’t a breeding programme, the problem is that even if DNA is banked at bio labs, there is still no proof needed to export cats such as with Cheetahs. There is not enough effort being put into the conservation of these majestic cats. We have not bio banked any of Chaos’ sperm yet.") Chaos and Teuqila are currently retired animals – who live in a lovely large cage at the back of the zoo where the public are not allowed. When animals become older and no longer enjoy the public – this is where they are brought to. Wild male lions usually only live to 10-12 years, while in captivity they can live from 20-24 years old.
metadata.Summary: Chaos is a 16 year old male tawny lion who has grown up in Midrand’s Lory Park Zoo. Weighing in at close to 300kg, this massive specimen came to the zoo in 2002 when he was a few weeks old. Back then there was no lion bone trade or lion pet industry – or the problems we currently have of a massive lion population in captivity in South Africa – which results in many going into the canned hunting industry. Lory park is a private zoo, that began when it’s owners Matty and Eddy van Eck wanted to share his private collection of animals - mostly birds with the public for educational purposes. They are a facility that brings in veterinary training students from overseas, and school students wanting to learn about animals up close and personal. They do not breed their animals now, but keep the females on contraception and the males are given vasectomy’s because this is better for the animal rather than outright neutering. This keeps the animals healthier – so they don’t gain excessive weight, and allows them to keep their natural tendency’s rather than just neutering them because it makes it easier for them to be handled. (Kara: "The reason that we use vasectomy is it is much less invasive and unfortunately the contraceptive implant has many negative affects on female cats. It also ensures that hormone levels aren’t affected.") Lory park was originally a bird park, based on the Lorikeet parrot – but it has grown to incorporate many other animals ranging from big cats, apes, reptiles and birds. Matty doesn’t see the animals as pets but as ambassadors for their kind and naturally has a deep love and respect for them - they have many conservation projects and work with Onderstepoort.
metadata.Further information: A few years ago one of their female tigers got cancer of her ovary’s and they tried all the veterinary options available, gave her life saving surgery, but in the end she didn’t survive (From Kara: unfortunately the cancer spread after a year and we made the very hard decision to let her go as her quality of life was being affected). When Chaos was diagnosed with skin cancer earlier this year, they were worried of losing him, most especially because of his bond with Tequila. He has skin cancer on his leg and nose, as lions love to lie in the sun. They were able to operate and remove much of the cancer in his leg because there’s lots of tissue, but his nose was a different matter. If they had left it, it would have eaten away his bones and face – causing him much suffering. Considering all the factors, what to do was a difficult decision, Matty and manager of the zoo Kara Heynis decided to try something different – radiation cancer treatment at a normal human hospital – rather than at a veterinary facility – mostly because Radiation on a male adult lion has never been tried before. (kara: "With regards to Chaos’ treatment we never decided to try something different. The veterinary team suggested that radiation would be the best way to treat his form of cancer and we proceeded with their recommendations after much consideration. This was a decision made by the parks management") This would be expensive, but as it’s a private facility they would get support from their private donors. Eddy had to make the decision with a lot of care, because once they did this for one animal, they would need to do it for every other, and they needed to make sure it wasn’t going to be too expensive that would result in the zoo closing its doors. They also wanted to give Chaos and Tequila time together, as they are inseparable, her wellbeing was also taken into consideration. This is the first time in South Africa that a male lion is being treated in a human hospital with a human doctor, and his oncologist at Meulmed private clinic in Pretoria Dr Ingo De Mûelenaere said after his first two treatments, the patient is doing very well. Overseen by Onderstepoort teaching sciences head Veterinarian Dr. Katja Koeppel, Chaos’ treatment is potentially a world first (although no one really knows – but I can’t find any other lion on the internet). His cancer treatment has gone viral with his pictures showing up in Asia, Australia, America and Europe! Dr. Koeppal and her team ensure that they use a light sedative on Chaos, because of his age, and because anaesthesia is always a concern for any animal, and they assist in transferring him from his sick bay at Lory Park, to Meulmed in Pretoria. Meulmed have been very accommodating, in that they close down their oncology bay during his visits. He is quite the attraction when he arrives, as you need to somehow get the big boy all the way onto the table, sedate him long enough to administer the radiation and then get him back into his personalized carrier – all as quick as possible so as to keep his stress down. We will be with him on his 3rd visit, after that he only has one more. After every radiation treatment the patient has made a full recovery, and is eating very well. Lions in captivity mostly die because they have kidney failure, but besides the cancer, Chaos has some of the most healthy bloods, and has been constantly monitored. We would tell Chaos’ personal story and show how difficult it is to give a fully grown male lion the best care he deserves.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: As there is a light sedative, if Chaos’ anxiety level increases the he won’t go under, so they’ve asked us not to be around him until after he’s out. Which is fine with us… we are welcome to film the entire process from start to finish, and I have secured Russell Bergh who is an animal specialist videographer who also used to be a Kruger ranger. They have also asked that we limit the number of people – I thought then potentially the best thing for us to do is to film half day from 3-7pm Wednesday next week (lions are better in the afternoon, by then Tequila won’t be on heat). They have housed Chaos is a special garden with lots of shade, lions love the sun, but because of his skin cancer and nose, they want him to be exposed to the sun as little as possible. We are welcome to go into his cage – heck no. and heck no is the presenter. Russell can do what he wants, but I choose life. I’m happy with just getting shots of him from a safe distance with a cage in-between lol. We can do Matty and Kara’s interviews by his cage, the vet’s interview on the day, and the oncologists interview on the day. There are only 4 interviews – which I think is fine for a 6 minute story. So it would be a day and a half shoot – if that’s fine? But I would ask that we only have the soundman on the half day at the facility, on the day of the actual moving etc it will just be me presenter and cameraman – so that there are fewer people. I will take full responsibility like I did in the pedigree dog story where we had no audio issues.
